extra.message: SQL injection in the /search route. The 'search' query parameter (request.args.get('search') at line 27) is interpolated directly into a SQLAlchemy text() clause: text(f"text like '%{search_param}%'"). An attacker can inject arbitrary SQL, e.g. search=' OR 1=1 -- , to read or modify database contents.

SQL injection in validate_token(), used by the /signup POST route. The user-supplied registration code (form.registration_code.data) is concatenated directly into a raw SQL statement: WHERE code = '{code}' inside session.execute(text(...)). An attacker can inject arbitrary SQL via the registration_code form field.

Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI) in the 404 error handler. render_template_string is called on an f-string that includes the attacker-controlled request.path. A request to a URL such as /%7B%7B7*7%7D (which decodes to /{{7*7}}) causes Jinja2 to evaluate the injected expression, enabling arbitrary code execution (e.g. {{ config }} or RCE payloads).

Insecure deserialization of the 'preferences' cookie using pickle.loads (loads imported from pickle at line 1). Any unauthenticated visitor can supply a crafted base64-encoded pickle in the cookie, which is deserialized on every request in the before_request hook, enabling remote code execution.

IDOR / broken access control in GET /accounts/<int:user_id>/notes. The route queries notes for the user_id taken from the URL without verifying that user_id matches current_user.id. Any authenticated user can enumerate and read other users' notes, including private ones (no 'private' filter is applied), by changing user_id in the URL.

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: IDOR / missing ownership check in POST /notes/<int:note_id>/delete. The note is fetched by note_id (session.get(Note, note_id)) and deleted without verifying note.user_id == current_user.id. Any authenticated user can delete arbitrary notes belonging to other users (the check in home.html line 41 only hides the UI button; the route itself has no authorization check).

cwe: CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key

extra.message: Privilege escalation via mass assignment in POST /account (update_account). AccountForm includes an 'is_admin' BooleanField, and current_user.__dict__.update(filtered_values) copies all form fields (including is_admin) onto the user object before session.merge/commit. A non-admin user can POST is_admin=true (or 'y') to the /account endpoint and grant themselves administrator privileges.

cwe: CWE-915: Improperly Controlled Modification of Dynamically-Determined Object Attributes

extra.message: Missing authentication on POST /account (update_account). Unlike the GET /account route (which has @login_required) and all other account routes, update_account performs account modifications without @login_required, allowing unauthenticated requests to reach the account-update logic.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: Stored XSS via the 'safe' filter. Note text is entered through a CKEditor rich-text field (partials/create_note_modal.html) and stored unsanitized by routes/notes.py add_note; it is then rendered with {{ note.text | safe }}, which disables Jinja2 autoescaping. Any user can create a note containing JavaScript that executes in other users' browsers viewing /home (notes are shared across users via utils/notes.py).

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

extra.message: Stored XSS via render_table with safe_columns=['text']. Note text is user-controlled rich text (CKEditor) stored without sanitization, and the 'text' column is marked safe (unescaped) when rendered in the search results table, allowing script injection.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

extra.message: Stored XSS via render_table with safe_columns=['text']. Note text is user-controlled rich text (CKEditor) stored without sanitization, and the 'text' column is rendered unescaped in the personal notes table, allowing script injection.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

extra.message: Server-Side Request Forgery in the profile image feature. The URL submitted to POST /account/image (routes/account.py lines 60-61 calls get_base64_image_blob(form.url.data)) is passed directly to urllib.request.urlopen with no scheme or host validation. An attacker can make the server fetch internal resources (e.g. http://169.254.169.254/ cloud metadata, internal services) or read local files via file:// URLs, with the content stored and displayed as the profile image.

XSS via profile image data URI. The mimetype for the profile image blob is derived from the attacker-controlled URL extension (guess_type(url)) and the downloaded content is not validated as an image. A user can point the image URL at a .html resource, producing a data:text/html;base64,... value that is rendered inside an <object data=...> tag in templates/home.html, base.html, and account.html, causing script execution in victims' browsers.

cwe: CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting')

extra.message: Hardcoded Flask secret key ("super secret key"). The key signs session cookies; anyone who knows it (it is in the public source) can forge session cookies and impersonate any user, including admins, bypassing authentication.

Hardcoded static registration code 'a36e990b-0024-4d55-b74a-f8d7528e1764' is seeded into the database. Anyone with access to the source can use this code to register an account via /signup without an admin-issued code.

Hardcoded default credentials: the database is seeded with user@evfa.com / 'user' and admin@evfa.com / 'admin' (including an admin account). These well-known weak credentials allow anyone to log in, including as the admin user.

SQLAlchemy engine is created with echo=True, which logs all SQL statements (including user-supplied values such as emails, registration codes, and note contents) to stdout/stderr. This leaks sensitive information into logs (CWE-532).

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: Denial of Service via unbounded resource consumption in the profile image download. urlopen(url) is called without a timeout and response.read() reads the entire response into memory with no size limit; a logged-in user can point /account/image at a very large or slow resource to exhaust server memory or hang worker processes.

Missing CSRF protection on POST /login (do_login). All forms in this app are plain wtforms.Form instances (not flask_wtf.FlaskForm) and the templates contain no CSRF tokens, so an attacker site can silently log a victim into an attacker-controlled account (login CSRF) via a cross-site POST.
Missing CSRF protection on POST /signup (do_signup). The registration form uses wtforms.Form with no CSRF token, allowing an attacker site to sign a victim up for an account via a cross-site POST.

Missing CSRF protection on POST /notes (add_note). The note creation form (partials/create_note_modal.html) contains no CSRF token, so an attacker site can create notes in a victim's name via a cross-site POST, including injecting stored-XSS payloads.

Missing CSRF protection on POST /notes/<note_id>/delete (delete_note). Combined with the missing ownership check on this route, an attacker site can force any logged-in victim's browser to delete arbitrary notes via a cross-site POST.

Missing CSRF protection on POST /account/image (add_image). The image URL form (partials/change_image_modal.html) has no CSRF token, so an attacker site can change a victim's profile image URL via a cross-site POST, triggering SSRF/XSS payloads under the victim's session.

Missing CSRF protection on POST /account (update_account). The account form (templates/account.html) contains no CSRF token, so an attacker site can modify a victim's account (email, password, is_admin) via a cross-site POST, enabling account takeover and privilege escalation.

Missing CSRF protection on POST /darkmode (toggle_darkmode). The preferences form (templates/account.html) has no CSRF token, allowing an attacker site to toggle a victim's preferences cookie via a cross-site POST.
